column4: The smallest length that means anything. Below this, distance itself stops making sense.
No experiment has ever found a quark to have any size at all. This is only the room it moves in.
Three quarks, and the force between them. Almost all the mass is that force, not the quarks.
Six protons and six neutrons, packed as tight as matter goes. Every atom of you is built around one of these.
The nucleus is the dot in the middle. The rest is electrons, and the rest is almost all of it.
One oxygen, two hydrogens, at an angle of 104.5 degrees. That angle is why water behaves as it does.
Two metres of this is coiled inside nearly every cell you have.
A shell of protein around a set of instructions. Too small to be alive on its own.
One cell, no nucleus, and more of these live on you than you have cells of your own.
Dished on both sides to carry more oxygen. You make about two million of them every second.
Thin enough to be a byword for thin, and still ten times a red blood cell.
The smallest thing you can pick up and look at.
The smallest thing that walks about with a plan.
The part of you that made everything else on this ladder.
You are here, almost exactly halfway between the smallest thing and the largest.
The largest animal that has ever lived, with a person beside it.
The size of a thing you can see all of, standing still.
The tallest things people build, still less than a thousandth of the air above them.
The highest ground on Earth, and a smaller bump than it feels from below.
Millions of lives, and from here only the lights.
A country, seen the way weather sees it.
The only other ground anyone has stood on.
Everything anyone has ever done, apart from a few days, happened here.
Eleven Earths across, and made of almost nothing but the two lightest gases.
A million Earths would fit inside. The dot is Earth, to scale.
Light takes eight minutes to cross from the middle to here.
Out to Neptune. Everything you have ever seen with your own eyes sits inside this circle, bar the stars.
A shell of ice around the Sun, a thousand times further out than the planets. The comets come from here.
The Sun is one of these. The next one along is four light years away, and that is close.
Stars being made, right now, and near enough to see with your eyes on a dark night.
A million old stars held together since the galaxy was young.
A few hundred billion stars. Every star you have ever seen by eye is one of them, and all of them are nearby.
Our galaxy, Andromeda, and about eighty smaller ones, falling towards each other.
A thousand galaxies. The beam is M87's jet, thrown five thousand light years by a black hole.
A hundred thousand galaxies, all drifting the same way. The name means immeasurable heaven.
Galaxies string along filaments, and between them the voids are almost perfectly empty.
As far as light has had time to reach us. The edge is the glow left over from the beginning.
